title_en: Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, Chief Investment Officer Americas and Head of Global Equities,
title_zh: Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi（UBS 美洲区 CIO 兼全球股票主管）：AI 是所有资产类别共同的隐藏因子
subtitle_zh: UBS 美洲区 CIO 回顾 Tudor 25 年交易教训，拆解三镜头组合框架与 AI 资本开支、隐藏因子的压力测试。
description: Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, Chief Investment Officer Americas and Head of Global Equities,

turns.en: Some of these secular trends, structural trends, have become macro factors, yet they're missing in most of the standard models. And the AI factor, in our view, needs to be a key element to stress test portfolios.
turns.zh: 其中一些长期趋势、结构性趋势，已经变成了宏观因子，但在大多数标准模型里它们是缺席的。我们认为，AI 因子应该成为组合压力测试的一个关键要素。

turns.en: Because if you just look at asset class buckets, you could easily think you're well diversified. You know, if, for example, you own a large cap tech stock, you own a utility, you own a real estate investment trust, you own emerging markets, and your own commodities.
turns.zh: 因为如果你只看资产类别的格子，你很容易觉得自己分散得很好。比如，你持有一只大盘科技股、一只公用事业股、一只 REIT（房地产投资信托，real estate investment trust）、新兴市场，还有大宗商品。

turns.en: That looks on the surface if you do a pie charge, right by asset class, like a well diversified portfolio. Yet, when you look underneath the surface, they all have one common hidden factor, and that is AI.
turns.zh: 表面上看，如果你按资产类别做一张饼图，它很像一个个分散良好的组合。但往水面之下看，它们全都共享同一个隐藏因子，那就是 AI。

turns.en: Hello, this is Dean Kernott, and welcome to the Alpha Exchange, where we explore topics in financial markets associated with managing risk, generating return, and the deployment of capital in the alternative investment industry.
turns.zh: 你好，我是 Dean Kernott，欢迎收听 Alpha Exchange。在这档节目里，我们探讨金融市场的各类话题，涵盖风险管理、回报创造，以及另类投资行业的资本配置。

turns.en: My guest today on the Alpha Exchange is Ulrike Hoppen-Bachardi. She is the CIO for the Americas and Global Head of Equities at UBS, Wealth Management.
turns.zh: 今天请到 Alpha Exchange 的嘉宾是 Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi，她是 UBS 财富管理的美洲区 CIO（首席投资官）兼全球股票主管。

turns.en: Ulrike, it's a pleasure to have you on the podcast today. It's a pleasure to be with you, Dean, after such a great macro mind conference just a few months ago.
turns.zh: Ulrike，今天很高兴请你来上播客。——我也很开心和你聊天，Dean，就在几个月前那场特别精彩的 Macro Minds 大会之后。

turns.en: It's going to be a great conversation. Let's start with your academic training, your background. You have a PhD in economics and political science, and boy, as you look around the world and you see some of the state craft that's going on in markets right now.
turns.zh: 今天的对话一定会很有收获。我们先从你的学术训练和背景聊起。你拥有经济学和政治学的博士学位——天哪，看看如今这个世界，看看市场上正在上演的种种政治手腕（statecraft），

turns.en: What an interesting area of study for your PhD. I'd love to start there. Take us all the way back to your academic training. Yeah, it's always funny when you look back what's been the red threat in your education and your professional career.
turns.zh: 你的博士课题真是太有意思了。我想就从这里开始，带我们回到你学术训练的起点。——是啊，回头看求学和职业生涯里那条一以贯之的主线，总是挺有意思的。

turns.en: And I think for me, it's been this innate curiosity of what comes next. And we talked earlier, you mentioned this idea of that the only constant is change and that you can't stand in the same river twice.
turns.zh: 对我来说，我觉得那是一种与生俱来的好奇心：接下来会发生什么。我们之前聊过，你提到过一个观点——唯一不变的就是变化本身，人不能两次踏进同一条河流。

turns.en: And I think that's always fascinated me. Changes in technology and economics. What ripple effects do those have for industries and also the markets more broadly?
turns.zh: 这一点一直让我着迷。技术和经济的变迁，会给行业、也会给更广泛的市场带来什么样的涟漪效应？

turns.en: And I've been drawn to this very early. In fact, my master thesis at the University of St. Gallen was on the industry convergence from the multimedia industry.
turns.zh: 我很早就被这个题目吸引了。实际上，我在圣加仑大学（University of St. Gallen）的硕士论文写的就是多媒体行业的产业融合。

turns.en: At the time, this was in the nineties, you had audio, text, video converging. And that posed real threats for three distinct industries, the computer industry.
turns.zh: 那是九十年代，当时音频、文字、视频正在融合。这对三个原本各自独立的行业构成了实实在在的威胁，第一个是计算机行业，

turns.en: That's what we call it at the time, media industry, and also the telco industry. It was an incredible threat to those incumbents. And if we look back at that time, we see how disruptive this multimedia industry, which was the precursor for the internet, actually was.
turns.zh: 那是我们当时的叫法；然后是媒体行业；还有电信行业。这对当时的在位巨头是巨大的威胁。回头看那个年代，你会发现多媒体这个行业——它其实是互联网的前奏——的颠覆性有多强。

turns.en: We talk a lot about the Mac 7 right now. Back then, the Mac 7 were IBM, Intel, Hewlett Packard, DEC. Not many people remember probably the company got later acquired by Hewlett Packard, but it was Digital Equipment Core, AT&T, Apple, and Microsoft.
turns.zh: 我们现在经常聊 Mag 7（美股七大科技巨头）。当年的 Mag 7 是 IBM、Intel、Hewlett-Packard、DEC。可能没多少人记得 DEC，它后来被 Hewlett-Packard 收购了，但它当时叫 Digital Equipment Corp；还有 AT&T、Apple 和 Microsoft。

turns.en: And really, of those seven, only two are now in the Mac 7 today. So it just shows you that these technology trends, they created enormous, of course, economic growth.
turns.zh: 这七家里，今天只剩两家还在 Mag 7 之列。所以你看，这些技术趋势确实创造了巨大的经济增长——

turns.en: The internet, digital economy is a large part of the US and world economy now, but it's also very disruptive and changes leadership in the market.
turns.zh: 互联网、数字经济如今已经占美国和世界经济很大的比重。但它同时也极具颠覆性，不断改变市场里的领导者。

turns.en: And I think for me, that was a first very good insight and one that stuck with me for the rest of my professional life. You use the term disruption, and I think it would be difficult to understate how much disruption today's world is characterized by.
turns.zh: 我觉得那是我早期的一个非常好的洞见，并且贯穿了我整个职业生涯。——你用了颠覆（disruption）这个词，我觉得当今世界被颠覆所主宰的程度，再怎么强调都不为过，

turns.en: And that, of course, yields both great opportunities and threats as well. I want to go back to this study of the intersection of political science and economics.
turns.zh: 而这当然既带来巨大的机会，也带来威胁。我想回到你研究政治学与经济学交叉点的那段经历。

turns.en: So it's several decades ago where you were engaged in this on an academic side. And yet the last couple of decades has just rewritten so many things just in terms of the geopolitical chessboard, the manner of central banking.
turns.zh: 你从学术角度介入这个领域已经是几十年前的事了。而过去这几十年，太多东西被重写了——地缘政治的棋盘、央行运作的方式。

turns.en: When you got this PhD, negative interest rates weren't a thing. The kind of world updates itself as technologies change, as the focus of governments change.
turns.zh: 你拿博士学位那会儿，负利率还不是一个概念。随着技术变化、政府关注点变化，世界自己也在更新。

turns.en: If you go back to that period in terms of your academic pursuits, where was the area of focus in trying to marry political science and economics?
turns.zh: 如果我们回到你做学术的那个阶段，在试图把政治学和经济学结合起来的尝试中，你的关注点在哪里？

turns.en: For me, actually, the allure, even of doing a PhD was to be at the forefront, or at least part of the forefront, the cutting edge of a area, even if it's very narrowly defined.
turns.zh: 对我来说，读博的吸引力其实在于站在某个领域的前沿，或者至少是前沿的一部分，哪怕这个领域定义得非常窄。

turns.en: For me, actually, it was econometrics, financial econometrics. That happened to also, through that lens, somewhat expose me, or at least give me opportunity to learn about what was the frontier of AI at that point.
turns.zh: 对我而言，那个领域其实是计量经济学、金融计量经济学。而透过这个视角，它也恰好让我接触到——或者至少给了我机会去了解——当时的 AI 前沿是什么。

turns.en: That was machine learning. That experience using statistics to understand financial phenomena actually ended up to be my entry ticket into the investing world with tutor investment.
turns.zh: 那就是机器学习。用统计学去理解金融现象的这段经历，最后反而成了我进入投资界的敲门砖，让我加入了 Tudor Investment。

turns.en: When you actually study financial economics or econometrics, you learn pretty quickly that the most challenging laboratory is not academia, but some markets themselves.
turns.zh: 当你真正研究金融经济学或计量经济学时，你会很快意识到，最有挑战性的实验室不是学术界，而是市场本身。

turns.en: For me, that was the catalyst to join Wall Street. Initially, the city of London, and maybe you're not the city of London because the tutor offices were located in Surrey in the south-west of London.
turns.zh: 对我来说，那就是去 Wall Street 的催化剂。最初是在 London 的金融城，不过也许不该说是金融城，因为 Tudor 的办公室在 London 西南边的 Surrey。

turns.en: Those were the first offices I worked in when I joined tutor in 1999. Let's talk about your long tenure at tutor managing capital. I find Paul Tudor Jones to be such an inspiring person in not just markets, but in his philanthropy.
turns.zh: 1999 年我加入 Tudor 时，第一批工作的办公室就是那里。——我们来聊聊你在 Tudor 管理资本的漫长任期吧。我觉得 Paul Tudor Jones 是个特别鼓舞人心的人，不只在市场里，也在慈善事业上。

turns.en: You and I have talked about that as well. He was on a podcast recently, and I listened to, and he was talking about trading silver in the early 1980s, and the Hunt Brothers effectively cornering the market.
turns.zh: 你我以前也聊过这个话题。他最近上了一期播客，我听了，他在聊八十年代初交易白银，以及 Hunt Brothers 几乎垄断逼仓的那段往事。

turns.en: His quote just sort of knocked me off my chair, which was, one of the Hunt Brothers was the richest person in the world by a factor of 3x, at least for a period of time when they ramped up silver and then it all came crashing down.
turns.zh: 他那句话真把我从椅子上震下来了：他说 Hunt Brothers 里有一位曾经是世界上最有钱的人，富出至少三倍——至少在他们把白银推高的那段时间是这样，随后一切轰然崩塌。

turns.en: I'd love to learn about your time at tutor, some of the lessons in managing capital at tutor. Yeah, I probably couldn't have started at a better place than tutor in 1999.
turns.zh: 我很想听听你在 Tudor 的岁月，以及在 Tudor 管理资本学到的一些教训。——我想，1999 年我很难找到比 Tudor 更好的起点了。

turns.en: And I thought it was going to be my first job, and I ended up there and spent almost 25 years at tutor. And it was really an extraordinary period of time.
turns.zh: 本来以为那只是我的第一份工作，结果一待就是将近 25 年。那真是一段非凡的岁月。

turns.en: And one, I would say probably the best investment experience that I could have gotten on Wall Street, starting off with Quant Macro, then Global Tactic Class at our location, built together with a colleague of mine, the Quant Equity business at tutor.
turns.zh: 可以说，那大概是我在 Wall Street 能得到的最好的投资经历：从量化宏观（Quant Macro）开始，然后是全球战术资产类别；我还和一位同事一起，在 Tudor 从零搭建起量化股票业务。

turns.en: And then last 14 years, I was responsible for the fundamental global equity portfolio and the flagship fund. So, so many different investment lenses.
turns.zh: 最后 14 年，我负责基本面全球股票组合和旗舰基金。那么多完全不同的投资视角。

turns.en: And I have to say, joining tutor from academia, you may be surprised that at the time, it was when I joined, and still is, the Champions League of academia.
turns.zh: 我必须说，从学术界加入 Tudor——你可能会惊讶——在我加入的时候（现在也还是），Tudor 简直就是学术界的欧冠联赛。

turns.en: There was so much intellectual firepower in the team. I remember one of my colleagues had a book just on his desk, casually, The Millennium Problems, The Seven Unsolved Math and Science Problems.
turns.zh: 团队里有那么多智力火力。我记得一位同事桌上就随手放着一本书，《千年难题：七个未解的数学与科学问题》（The Millennium Problems）。

turns.en: One of them has been solved since then. It was not for casual reading, in his case. Hey, you would win a million dollars if you solved one of those.
turns.zh: 其中一个问题后来已经被解决了。对他来说，那可不是休闲读物。嘿，解决其中一个可是能赢一百万美元的。

turns.en: That was the type of environment, discussing the Fermi paradox, causality, correlation, even singularity back then. A period where there was so much curiosity, it sparked my own curiosity in learning about new things and also a breadth of just topics that you weren't exposed to, maybe necessarily on Wall Street.
turns.zh: 就是那样的环境——讨论 Fermi 悖论、因果与相关，甚至在当年就聊奇点（singularity）。那是一个好奇心爆棚的时期，点燃了我自己学新东西的热情，也带来特别宽的话题面——这些在 Wall Street 未必一定接触得到。

turns.en: But like you said, Paul makes a big, big difference. He truly has created a very unique culture at tutor, investing or even trading. Is it challenging psychological proposition?
turns.zh: 但就像你说的，Paul 带来了非常大的、非常大的不同。他真正在 Tudor 创造出一种非常独特的文化。投资，甚至交易，本质上是一个很有挑战性的心理学命题，不是吗？

turns.en: Kahneman Twesky, I always loved their finding that when you experience a loss in trading, it's twice as painful as the equivalent gain gives you joy.
turns.zh: Kahneman 和 Tversky，我一直特别喜欢他们的发现：当你在交易里经历一笔亏损，它的痛苦是同等盈利带来快乐的两倍。

turns.en: So that two-to-one ratio is pretty challenging. Paul's magic is that he improved that ratio with a great culture and always a little bit of fun on the trading day.
turns.zh: 所以这个 2:1 的比例是相当难缠的。Paul 的魔力在于，他用非常好的文化把这个比例改善了，再加上交易日里总有一点乐趣。

turns.en: I think that also is the reason why so many people have stayed so long at tutor and the 10 years of portfolio managers is probably much longer than the industry average.
turns.zh: 我想这也是为什么那么多人在 Tudor 待了那么久——这里组合经理大约 10 年的任职时长，可能远长于行业平均水平。

turns.en: One thing he talks a lot about is drawdowns. They're inevitable. As you, I think, are lewd to there, take a psychological toll. Loss is hurt, not just the economics of them, but the psyche impact.
turns.zh: 他经常谈的一个话题是回撤（drawdown）。回撤不可避免，我想你也提到过，它们会带来心理上的消耗。亏损不只伤在经济上，更伤在心态上。

turns.en: And I'm just curious if you can share with us some lessons that you may have taken away from your experience at tutor, managing through the difficult times, maybe trying to re-underwrite your process along the way.
turns.zh: 我很好奇，你能不能和我们分享一下，你在 Tudor 的经历里带走的一些教训——怎么穿越艰难时期，一路上怎么重新审视、重新校验你的流程。

turns.en: Walk us through some of those periods. I think the biggest lesson for me or the biggest takeaway from my whole 25 years there was this one quote is that there's nothing new under the sun.
turns.zh: 带我们走一遍那些时期吧。——我想，对我来说，在那儿整整 25 年最大的教训、最大的收获，就是这么一句话：太阳底下无新事。

turns.en: It's actually a quote from the book Reminisances of a Stock Operator that shares the biography of Jesse Livermore, this prolific trader in the early 1900s.
turns.zh: 这句话其实出自《股票作手回忆录》（Reminiscences of a Stock Operator），这本书讲的是 Jesse Livermore 的生平，他是二十世纪初非常高产的交易员。

turns.en: It's a book that Paul gives to every new trader at the firm. He gave it to everyone 25 plus years ago and still today. I think what he means is that the human emotions or the pendulum of human emotions swings between fear and greed, and that is a constant.
turns.zh: 这本书 Paul 会送给公司每一位新交易员。二十多年前他就送给我，今天依然在送。我理解他的意思是：人类情绪这座钟摆在恐惧与贪婪之间摆动，这是唯一不变的常量。

turns.en: History might not repeat exactly, but it rhymes. And those two spectrums or those two ends of the spectrum of human emotions very much manifest themselves in the markets.
turns.zh: 历史未必精确重复，但它会押韵。人类情绪光谱的这两个极端，在市场里体现得淋漓尽致。

turns.en: You mentioned silver, there's been so many market episodes where we have gotten to points of maybe irrational exuberance or short-term exuberance that then corrected pretty violently.
turns.zh: 你提到了白银。有太多市场桥段，我们曾到达非理性繁荣——或者说是短期狂热——的顶点，然后出现非常剧烈的修正。

turns.en: And I think Paul in particular has a unique skill in detecting when there's opportunities arise and also size appropriately at those times. This is maybe another way of just saying that analog studies in the markets are something that is very important.
turns.zh: 我想 Paul 尤其有一种独特的本事：察觉到机会何时出现，并且在那个时点把仓位规模配到位。你这其实也是另一种说法：市场里的类比研究（analog studies）非常重要。

turns.en: From that come three other trading lessons or pieces of trading advice or insight that I've taken away. One is in every Tudorite who sat on the trading floor with Paul has heard that multiple times, but the trend is your friend.
turns.zh: 由此我带走了另外三条交易教训或者说心得。第一条，每一个在交易大厅和 Paul 一起坐过的 Tudor 人都听过无数遍：趋势是你的朋友（the trend is your friend）。

turns.en: Be prepared to write trends. But I think he combines that with a really unique ability to also sell negative convexity and not just once, but he's done that over and over again.
turns.zh: 但要准备好驾驭趋势。我觉得他把这一点和另一种真正独特的能力结合在一起，那就是卖出负凸性（negative convexity）——不止一次，而是一次又一次。

turns.en: And then second, that sizing matters and trade expression matters. So you might not need a 60% hit ratio if you can size appropriately at the right time.
turns.zh: 第二条是，仓位大小很重要，交易的表达方式也很重要。所以你不一定需要 60% 的胜率，只要能在正确的时点把仓位配得恰当。

turns.en: If you have conviction, you have to go large. And there are ways at times where you can express that through options in a very, very risk-aware way.
turns.zh: 如果你有信念，就要下重注。而且有些时候，你可以通过期权来表达观点，用一种对风险非常、非常敏感的方式。

turns.en: And then I would say the last thing is that liquidity matters. We have seen over and over again that certain times in the markets we think that certain products are liquid only in times of duress to find out that there's suddenly no bid.
turns.zh: 最后一条是，流动性很重要。我们一次又一次看到，在市场里某些时刻，我们以为某些产品流动性很好，只有在承压的时候才发现，突然之间没人出价了。

turns.en: So stress testing portfolio through liquidity lens is one of the third big lessons that I've taken away from that period. When you look back again on your tenure there, markets, they teach us things.
turns.zh: 所以从流动性的视角去压力测试组合，是我从那段时期带走第三个重要教训。——再回看你在那里的任期，市场确实教会我们很多东西。

turns.en: And it could be, as you say, the evaporation of liquidity at a time when you kind of needed it, whether it's a correlation flip, sign flip that was unexpected or unwelcome.
turns.zh: 可能就像你说的，流动性在你最需要它的时候蒸发；也可能是相关性的翻转、符号的翻转，来得出乎意料或者不受欢迎。

turns.en: As you kind of look back on that period, 1999 to 2020, boy, that's a lot of action. You've got debt crises. You've got the GFC itself. You've got some geopolitical motivating factors that have really moved markets.
turns.zh: 回头看那段时期，1999 年到 2020 年，天哪，那真是大戏连连。有债务危机，有全球金融危机（GFC）本身，还有很多真正驱动市场的地缘政治因素。

turns.en: And then, of course, COVID. Take us through maybe one or two specific periods where the markets were speaking to you and your team. You tried to maybe reposition the portfolio in light of how the market was communicating.
turns.zh: 然后当然还有新冠。带我们走一遍一两个具体的时期吧——市场在对你和你的团队说话，你根据市场传递的信息试着重新调整组合。

turns.en: Again, whether it was around correlation, whether it was around, hey, this is a new stress event we haven't seen before. So we've got to kind of get the portfolio back to home base.
turns.zh: 不管是围绕相关性，还是围绕这是一个我们没见过的新型压力事件，得把组合带回到安全基准线上。那些教训是什么？

turns.en: What are some of those lessons? Probably one of the overarching lessons is that it's so important to blend different perspectives. Macro is one very important perspective.
turns.zh: 我想最总的教训之一，是融合不同视角非常重要。宏观是一个非常重要的视角；

turns.en: The other one is the bottom-up fundamentals. So when we go back to this long period, there have been moments of crisis that have been triggered by company fundamentals, thinking back about Bear Stearns, Lehman, Silicon Valley Bank.
turns.zh: 另一个是自下而上（bottom-up）的基本面。回到这段漫长的时期，有过由公司基本面引发的危机时刻，想想 Bear Stearns、Lehman、Silicon Valley Bank。

turns.en: Understanding the balance sheet of companies is very important. If you detect asset liability mismatches, that is a sign of vulnerability. But on the other side, you need to understand the macro.
turns.zh: 理解公司的资产负债表非常重要。如果你能发现资产与负债的错配，那就是脆弱性的信号。但反过来，你也需要理解宏观。

turns.en: And certainly the powered pivot in December 21 was a very important signal for the equity markets, especially in the macro firm. Having both of those perspectives is really important to navigate those moments.
turns.zh: 比如 2021 年 12 月 Powell 的态度转向，对股票市场就是一个非常重要的信号，尤其对我们这样的宏观型机构。同时具备这两个视角，对驾驭那些时刻真的非常重要。

turns.en: I would say that not having blind spots by having different PMs with different focus areas that are coming together in joint meetings is very important.
turns.zh: 我会说，让关注点不同的多位组合经理在联席会议上聚在一起、从而没有盲区，这非常重要。

turns.en: The famous computer scientist Alan Kay likes to say that perspective is worth more than 80 IQ points. So the more perspectives you can bring together, I think the higher the overall intelligent IQ pool of the firm.
turns.zh: 著名的计算机科学家 Alan Kay 有句话：视角胜过 80 个 IQ 点。你能汇聚的视角越多，一家机构整体智力池的上限就越高。

turns.en: It's so interesting that as you talk about perspective, perspective is gained through time. I mean, there's just kind of no substitute for it.
turns.zh: 特别有意思的是，你一直在讲视角，而视角是靠时间换来的。它真的没有什么替代品。

turns.en: The unwind of the portfolio this summer, a month ago, you put a lot of capital in the hands of someone that clearly had tremendously interesting insights on AI.
turns.zh: 今年夏天、一个月前的那轮组合撤仓，你把大量资金交给了一个显然对 AI 有非常独到见解的人，

turns.en: But at 25 years old, it's just hard to gather a lot of perspective along the way. That's at least the opinion of some folks. So you have the benefit of a long career here.
turns.zh: 但 25 岁的年纪，一路走来很难积累多少视角——至少一些人是这么看的。所以你这边的优势是漫长的职业生涯。你在 Tudor 待了几十年，然后转到 UBS。跟我们讲讲全球股票 CIO 这个角色吧，

turns.en: You were at Tudor for decades and made this move to UBS. Tell us about the role as CIO for global equities. Then we'll dive into a lot of how you're thinking about portfolio construction right now.
turns.zh: 然后我们再深入聊很多你现在怎么思考组合构建的问题。

turns.en: So the role at UBS is just broader and in two ways. One is more scale and then also more breadth in terms of coverage. As CIO in America, we cover all asset classes private and public and then the same for global equities.
turns.zh: UBS 这个角色在两个维度上更宽：一是规模，二是覆盖的广度。作为美洲区 CIO，我们覆盖所有资产类别，私募和公开市场都算；全球股票这边也是一样。

turns.en: We have, as UBS now, 7.3 trillion assets under management. So scale is always a dimension of how we think about investing. But also we have to understand all parts of the market, whether they're public or private, equity, credit, commodities.
turns.zh: UBS 现在的资产管理规模是 7.3 万亿美元。所以规模永远是我们思考投资的一个维度。而且我们必须理解市场的每一个部分，无论公开还是私募，股票、信用、大宗商品。

turns.en: And it's a huge opportunity to bring all these different perspectives of the different investing and analyst teams together to help us understand where we should be positioned, but also where there are risk factors.
turns.zh: 这是一个巨大的机会：把各个投资和分析师团队的不同视角汇聚起来，帮我们理解自己应该站在什么位置，也理解风险因子在哪里。

turns.en: I would say that CIO is a little bit of a lighthouse for UBS, setting the investment direction, but making sure that we also navigate carefully the risks that are out there, but also making sure that we get comedy to our destination, which is still aligning our portfolios to the biggest long-term investing opportunities.
turns.zh: 我会说，CIO 有点像 UBS 的灯塔，负责设定投资方向，同时确保我们谨慎地规避前方的风险，也确保我们载着客户抵达目的地——这个目的地，依然是把组合对齐到最大的长期投资机会上。

turns.en: Well, you had said this, I don't know if it was last time we spoke that risk and opportunity are kind of the same thing. And if you're in the world of investing, there's this constant push and pull of taking too much or too little risk.
turns.zh: 你说过这句话——我不确定是不是上次我们聊天时说的——风险和机会其实是同一件事。在做投资的世界里，永远存在风险 take 得太多还是太少的拉锯。

turns.en: One is a risk of a drawdown. Perhaps you've mis-sized your allocation and then you have to make a decision you don't want to cut risk. And the other was an opportunity cost, which is just not taking enough risk.
turns.zh: 一种是回撤的风险：你可能把某个配置的仓位定错了，然后就被迫做一个你并不想做的决定——削减风险。另一种是机会成本，也就是承担的风险不够。

turns.en: Both are challenging. That's where I really want to get into is just your portfolio, the process by which you're constructing portfolios on behalf of clients.
turns.zh: 两者都很难熬。所以我真正想聊的，就是你的组合本身，以及你代表客户构建组合的流程。

turns.en: Why don't you take us through the 30,000 feet of that right now? What sort of the portfolio looks like big picture? And then we can kind of drill down into some of the specific allocations.
turns.zh: 你能带我们以三千英尺的高度看一下现在的全貌吗？大画面下组合是什么样子？然后我们再下钻到一些具体的配置。

turns.en: Portfolio, construction, takes three things, right? One, expected returns. What do these investments earn? The risk or beach of these investments number two and then the correlations between these investments as a third.
turns.zh: 组合构建取决于三件事：第一，预期收益——这些投资能赚多少？第二，这些投资的风险或者说波动；第三，这些投资之间的相关性。

turns.en: And you take all these three things and you try to balance risk and reward in a way that is aligned with the client objectives. And we use a three lens framework for that.
turns.zh: 你把这三样东西放在一起，尝试以符合客户目标的方式去平衡风险与回报。我们为此使用一个三镜头（three lens）框架。

turns.en: We've talked before about macro and bottom-up. These two lenses are pretty common on Wall Street. You have macro investing teams and you have bottom-up teams, stock analysts, sector analysts and so forth.
turns.zh: 我们以前聊过宏观和自下而上。这两个镜头在 Wall Street 相当常见：你有宏观投资团队，也有自下而上的团队，股票分析师、行业分析师等等。

turns.en: We have both of these, but we also have a third lens that is different. And that's the lens of the structural trends. So those persistent trends that are going to create wealth in the economy, but also very importantly offer unique investment opportunities in how they transform the economies.
turns.zh: 这两个我们都有，但我们还有第三个不同的镜头，就是结构性趋势的镜头。那些持久的趋势不仅会在经济中创造财富，更重要的是，它们在改造经济的过程中提供了独特的投资机会。

turns.en: For us, that means three things, not surprisingly AI. The second is electrification, which we call power and resources. And the third is longevity.
turns.zh: 对我们来说，这意味着三件事，不意外：AI。第二个是电气化，我们把它叫作电力与资源（power and resources）。第三个是长寿（longevity）。

turns.en: We not only talk about these as investing opportunities, we've also structured our organization accordingly. According to these three lenses where we have top-down macro analysts, we have bottom-up stock analysts.
turns.zh: 我们不只是把这些当投资机会来谈，我们还按照这三个镜头重构了组织：我们自上而下有宏观分析师，自下而上有股票分析师，

turns.en: And then we have three teams globally that are focused on these three opportunities. And as you said, we use those in order to come up with our expected returns.
turns.zh: 另外还有三个全球团队分别聚焦这三个机会。正如你所说，我们用这些镜头来形成我们的预期收益判断。

turns.en: But at the same time, each of these buckets are also the lens of risk that we need to be aware of. For example, right now, when we think about risk, I always tend to start with the areas where there have been most inflow.
turns.zh: 但与此同时，这几个板块每一个也是我们需要注意的风险镜头。举个例子，现在当我们思考风险时，我总是习惯从资金流入最多的地方开始——

turns.en: Most excesses. And certainly what we have seen, of course, is on the one side, AI, we are seeing a massive CAPEX trajectory data center built out, which has, of course, become a macro factor of its own.
turns.zh: 最过热的地方。我们显然看到，一方面在 AI 上，巨大的资本开支（capex）轨迹和数据中心建设，本身已经成为一个宏观因子。

turns.en: So that's certainly one area to be very closely focused on. But the other area that's been, of course, lingering for some time is the incredible amount of public debt that's outstanding.
turns.zh: 所以那绝对是一个需要紧盯的领域。但另一个徘徊已久的领域，当然是天量的存量公共债务。

turns.en: The balance sheet of government is certainly much more stretched than the balance sheet of the largest CAP companies in the world. Those are the two lenses that we are primarily focused on when we think about risk.
turns.zh: 政府的资产负债表，肯定比全球最大市值公司的资产负债表紧绷得多。这两个镜头就是我们思考风险时最主要关注的。

turns.en: But all three, like we talked about before, could be used to construct expected return, but also scenarios of what happens if certain of these things are going to change.
turns.zh: 但就像我们刚才说的，三个镜头都可以用来构建预期收益，也可以用来推演情景——如果其中某些东西发生变化会怎样？

turns.en: How is the portfolio going to react if AI CAPEX turns to slow, if we don't see monetization quickly enough, and the same on the right side, what happened if we see more potential risk for the term premium spikes?
turns.zh: 如果 AI 资本开支开始放缓、如果变现（monetization）来得不够快，组合会怎么反应？同样地，如果期限溢价（term premium）飙升的潜在风险变大，会怎样？

turns.en: What happens to, for example, the CAPEX trajectory, the build out of more data centers if just financing costs are starting to become more strained?
turns.zh: 如果融资成本本身开始变得吃紧，资本开支的轨迹、更多数据中心的建设又会怎样？

turns.en: So those are some of the questions that we are primarily focused on when we think about portfolio construction. The back end of the bond market has become a real active topic of conversation.
turns.zh: 这些就是我们思考组合构建时最关注的问题。——债券市场的长端最近真成了大家热议的话题。

turns.en: I tend to just try to look at news headlines. I look at the FT in the Wall Street Journal and spend way too much time on the Bloomberg Terminal.
turns.zh: 我平时就是看看新闻头条，读读 FT 和 Wall Street Journal，花太多时间泡在 Bloomberg 终端上。

turns.en: You just don't want to see the coverage of the long end of the U.S. bond market framed the way it is currently. And then, of course, you've got Besant, pretty activist Treasury Secretary with a hedge fund background himself, intervening in certain ways, whether it's through the Yen, the Treasury buyback, and so forth.
turns.zh: 你肯定不想看到美国债券市场长端被现在这样报道。而且当然，还有 Bessent，一位相当活跃的财政部长，自己就有对冲基金背景，以各种方式介入，不管是日元、国债回购（Treasury buyback）等等。

turns.en: What would be the signal for you and your team that things on the back end are becoming vulnerable enough to start to impact the investment thesis on something like AI, where it's hard for the U.S. corporate economy to do really well if the long end of the bond market is particularly unruly?
turns.zh: 对你和你的团队来说，什么样的信号意味着长端已经脆弱到足以开始冲击 AI 这类主题的投资逻辑——因为如果债券市场长端特别不听话，美国企业经济很难真正过好？

turns.en: You're watching for that risk. What does that look like for you guys? Yeah, I think it's a question that's really critical for the market right now, and actually a question that also the Fed currently is facing.
turns.zh: 你们在盯着这个风险。从你们那边看，它长什么样？——是的，我觉得这真的是当下市场对整个行情最关键的问题之一，其实也是 Fed（美联储）目前面对的问题。

turns.en: It's somewhat caught in a silver and corruptist moment where for some parts of the economy, current rates are already restrictive. You think about the housing market and the data this week showed we are at a three and a half year low in terms of U.S. housing starts.
turns.zh: 它多少有点腹背受敌：对经济的某些部分来说，当前利率已经是限制性水平了。想想住房市场，本周数据显示美国的 housing starts（新屋开工）已经跌到三年半以来的低位。

turns.en: On the other side, we still have what seems to be very unconstrained AI capital expenditures. To your question is how much in terms of rate uplift do you need to see for that to slow?
turns.zh: 另一方面，AI 资本支出看起来仍然完全不受约束。回到你的问题：利率要抬到什么程度，才会让它慢下来？

turns.en: I do think it will take quite a bit, not 25-50 basis points. And the reason is that right now already these hyperscalers are paying three times the salary of an electrician to build the data center.
turns.zh: 我确实认为需要相当多的幅度，不是 25 到 50 个基点。原因是，现在这些超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）为了建数据中心，已经在付电工三倍于市场行情的工资。

turns.en: They're paying twice the base rate for electricity in order to build data centers. These are all data points that at this point suggest that the elasticity to rates or the rate elasticity of AI capex is very, very low.
turns.zh: 它们为了建数据中心，在付两倍于基准价电费。这些 datapoint 都说明，目前 AI 资本开支对利率的弹性（rate elasticity）非常、非常低。

turns.en: I think we need to see a lot more. However, at some point, there could also just be some sort of risk in the treasury market independently of the AI question.
turns.zh: 我觉得还需要看到更多才行。不过到某个时点，国债市场本身也可能出现某种风险，跟 AI 的问题无关。

turns.en: What if at some point confidence starts to seize that the U.S. is going to be able to repay its debt? Those are other moments of a confidence crisis that are probably independent of the AI built out.
turns.zh: 如果到某个时点，开始有人怀疑美国还债的能力、信心出现动摇呢？那些信心危机的时刻，大概跟 AI 建设本身是相互独立的。

turns.en: But at this point, in our view, the sensitivity is still pretty low and it probably will take more than 50 basis points to make a dent in that trajectory.
turns.zh: 但就现阶段而言，在我们看来，敏感度还是很低，可能得超过 50 个基点才会对那条轨迹造成实质性冲击。

turns.en: Because the price of AGI and to be the first in AGI could be very large. And all these companies that are now among the Mac 7, they have seen that movie before.
turns.zh: 因为通往 AGI 的代价、以及成为第一个到达 AGI 的玩家的回报可能非常大。而现在这几家 Mag 7 公司，都看过这部电影。

turns.en: How quickly you can be displaced by somebody entering the market and looking at it from a slightly different lens with a slightly different approach and taking share.
turns.zh: 一个带着略微不同的视角、略微不同的方法进入市场的后来者，可以多快抢走份额、取而代之。

turns.en: If we go back to this analogy of the 90s, we have since then a number of new companies emerge, the large digital platforms that have taken massive share from some of those incumbents.
turns.zh: 回到九十年代那个类比，从那以后涌现出一批新公司，也就是大型数字平台，从在位巨头手里抢走了巨大的份额。

turns.en: Google, Meta, Amazon, right? These are all companies that emerged in the 2000s and redefined the whole computer telco and media landscape. Knowing that AI is such a disruptive technology, we're seeing exponential increase in capabilities.
turns.zh: Google、Meta、Amazon，对吧？这些都是 2000 年代冒出来的公司，重新定义了计算机、电信和媒体的整个版图。既然 AI 是这样一种颠覆性技术，我们正看到它的能力呈指数级提升。

turns.en: It's very difficult to say, oh, just 25 basis points. That's too high in order to not participate in this game. So likely other risk factors are probably more front and center for us when it comes to the AI trade, such as are there bottlenecks in the supply chain?
turns.zh: 所以很难说，哦，25 个基点太高了，因此不去参与这场比赛。所以对 AI 交易来说，其他风险因素可能更靠前，比如供应链上有没有瓶颈？

turns.en: It's a quite sophisticated supply chain starting with the permitting. Are we going to get enough permits for data centers through? Probably a little bit of a slowdown heading into the midterm elections, given that we see so much political opposition now already even in the Republican primaries.
turns.zh: 这是一条相当复杂的供应链，从审批开始：数据中心的许可我们能不能批下来？随着中期选举临近，可能会有点放缓，因为现在甚至在共和党初选里就已经看到这么多政治反对。

turns.en: That's the question, are we going to see bottlenecks in electricity supply? Are we seeing bottlenecks in other areas of power generation? I think those are the key questions.
turns.zh: 问题就在这里：电力供应会不会出现瓶颈？发电的其他环节会不会出现瓶颈？我认为这些是关键问题。

turns.en: We anticipate in CIO that we are about 100 gigawatt short in electricity by 2030 in order to cater to the amount we're seeing, not just from AI, but also the built out of transportation, electrification infrastructure, building electrification infrastructure, and an electrical industrial footprint.
turns.zh: 我们在 CIO 预计，到 2030 年电力大约会短缺 100 吉瓦，才能满足我们看到的需求——不只是 AI，还有交通电气化基础设施、建筑电气化基础设施，以及工业电气化的铺开。

turns.en: So that means that there could be periods of time where we might be short turbines, transformers, certain electrical parts of the grid ecosystem.
turns.zh: 这意味着在某些时间段，我们可能会短缺涡轮机、变压器，以及电网生态系统的某些电气部件。

turns.en: Those are things to watch for on the supply side, but there could also be demand bottlenecks. How quickly can we absorb an organization, the incredible capabilities of AI?
turns.zh: 这些是供给侧要关注的事情，但需求侧同样可能有瓶颈：组织和机构消化 AI 惊人能力的速度有多快？

turns.en: And if we see that monetization doesn't increase at the extent that the market anticipates, that could be another risk factor to watch out for.
turns.zh: 如果我们看到变现的增长达不到市场预期的程度，那也可能是另一个需要警惕的风险因素。

turns.en: So those on the AI side, demand and supply bottlenecks are front and center. There are probably a few others that are being discussed in the market, such as the Chinese models, for example, that are much more efficient.
turns.zh: 所以在 AI 这边，需求和供给的瓶颈是最要紧的。市场上大概还有几个讨论因素，比如中国的模型，效率高得多。

turns.en: But in our view, that doesn't mean that we need fewer chips or fewer AI. That only means we'll have more AI because the cheaper AI gets, the more we're going to use it.
turns.zh: 但在我们看来，那并不意味着我们需要更少的芯片或者更少的 AI。它只会意味着更多的 AI——因为 AI 越便宜，我们就会用得越多。

turns.en: And I think there are so many use cases. We are just starting to scratch the surface. We have seen that coding now has become fully autonomous.
turns.zh: 而且我觉得用例多不胜数，我们才刚刚开始触及皮毛。我们已经看到，写代码现在完全自主化了。

turns.en: You're a developer now. You're barely watching a video where the code checks itself. The job that I started with a tutor where you write code in order to construct quantitative models that predict stocks and individual stocks and indices and so forth, that job doesn't even exist anymore.
turns.zh: 你现在更像开发者，基本是在旁边看着代码自我检查。我在 Tudor 做的第一份工作——写代码搭建量化模型来预测个股和指数——这个岗位甚至已经不存在了。

turns.en: And that properly happened in the period of five months. We have seen the breakthroughs in math almost on a daily basis. A new theorem is going to be rejected or another proof comes about that we couldn't come up with for 50 or 100 years.
turns.zh: 而这一切大概就是五个月里发生的事。我们几乎每天都能看到数学上的突破：新的定理被提出，又或者某个我们一百年都没想出来的难题出现了证明。

turns.en: We're seeing massive opportunity also in biochemistry, what AI means to drug discovery. So when you look at the price, it is just so large. It addresses probably at a lower boundary, at a minimum, the 50 trillion of knowledge worker salaries.
turns.zh: 我们还看到生物化学里巨大的机会，AI 对药物发现的意义。所以当你看看这个奖赏有多大——它至少触达的下限，是 50 万亿美元的知识工作者薪资。

turns.en: It's very difficult to believe that you would voluntarily give up to be part of this race. You make a really interesting point on the restrictiveness either for the different borrowers, the level of restrictiveness of rates.
turns.zh: 很难相信会有人主动放弃参与这场竞赛。——你关于利率限制性的点很有意思，对不同借款方，利率的限制程度是不一样的。

turns.en: So for a homeowner, and Morris has said this, it's restrictive. You're not going to get massively wealthy buying a house. Maybe it goes up a little bit, but you're dealing with a right tail situation on the AI front where the cost of capital is just overwhelmed by the prospects of reaching that right tail.
turns.zh: 对房主来说——Morris 也说过——现在是限制性的。买套房不会让你发大财，也许涨一点。但在 AI 这边，你面对的是一个右尾情形：资金成本完全被触及那个右尾的可能性压倒了。

turns.en: That cost of capital is unlikely high enough to slow the capex buildout at this point. On the bottlenecks notion, I love this way of thinking about in terms of both supply side and demand side bottlenecks, it's going to be inevitable.
turns.zh: 现阶段资金成本不太可能高到拖慢资本开支的建设。关于瓶颈这个概念，我很喜欢你这种从供给侧和需求侧两头看的思路。瓶颈的到来不可避免。

turns.en: It's just impossible for something to truly go up and to the right in a straight line. So these are coming to some extent. You've talked about trying to position around being on the upstream side versus the downstream side of the bottlenecks to find those assets in the supply chain that are less vulnerable to the bottlenecks.
turns.zh: 任何东西都不可能真的走一条直线一路向上。所以这些瓶颈在某种程度上总会来。你谈到过尽量站在瓶颈的上游还是下游来布局，在供应链里找到那些对瓶颈没那么脆弱的资产。

turns.en: What does that look like? Give us an area that's more vulnerable to what is inevitable, some bottleneck, and then those that should be slightly less vulnerable to a bottleneck.
turns.zh: 那具体长什么样？给我们举一个更容易被——不可避免——瓶颈所伤的例子，再举一个应该对瓶颈相对没那么脆弱的例子。

turns.en: One way that we think to position for what's to come, and we look at it through the three transformation innovations, AI and electrification longevity, is through dedicated portfolios in each one of those.
turns.zh: 我们为即将到来的变化布局的方式之一——透过 AI、电气化、长寿这三项变革性创新——是为每一项建立专门的组合。

turns.en: We call them the trios, the transformational innovation opportunities. So those are designed mainly to play offense, to position into these opportunities.
turns.zh: 我们把它们称为三驾马车（trios），也就是变革性创新的机会组合。它们的设计主要是为了打进攻，是为了押注这些机会。

turns.en: By the way, AI is the one fundamental connector of all three, because of course, you need power and resources in order to build data centers, to empower them, and then longevity is going to be a big beneficiary of AI with drug discovery, but also other parts of the healthcare value chain.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，AI 是这三者的根本连接点：当然，你需要电力和资源来建设并驱动数据中心；而长寿会受益于 AI 的很大一部分，无论是药物发现，还是医疗健康价值链的其他环节。

turns.en: So we have SEO portfolios that we recommend to our clients, to position for these opportunities, to play offense. But we always like to build in defense when we are playing offense as well.
turns.zh: 所以我们有专门的组合推荐给客户端，用来布局这些机会、打进攻。但我们在打进攻的同时，总想配一些防守。

turns.en: So even in the parts of the portfolio that are aligned to the structural opportunities, we want to build in some balance. And that in our case means some diversification in how we are playing offense.
turns.zh: 因此即使是在对齐结构性机会的那部分组合里，我们也想建立某种平衡。对我们来说，这意味着在进攻方式上做分散。

turns.en: And also a dynamism in how we are playing offense, because we've talked about how quickly AI is changing, where the bottlenecks may occur, where we may see oversupply.
turns.zh: 同时也意味着进攻要有动态调整，因为我们聊过 AI 变化有多快、瓶颈可能出现在哪里、哪里可能出现供给过剩。

turns.en: We can adjust our portfolios according to our analysis of the demand and supply along the AI value chain in particular. In the AI portfolio, we can position along the whole AI value chain, the enablers, the picks and shovels, the chip companies, the networking companies, and so forth.
turns.zh: 我们可以根据对 AI 价值链上供需的分析来调整组合。在 AI 组合里，我们可以整条 AI 价值链布局：使能层（enablers）、卖铲子的（picks and shovels）、芯片公司、网络设备公司等等。

turns.en: In the intelligence layer, companies who are at the frontier of intelligence or the application layer, the company is using AI and apply them, whether it's to advertising, whether it's to just enterprise productivity and so forth.
turns.zh: 智能层（intelligence layer），站在智能前沿的公司；或者应用层（application layer），使用和落地 AI 的公司，无论是用于广告，还是用于企业生产力等等。

turns.en: So it gives us a way to play defense also. We think certain areas, for example, of semiconductors have outrun their pores or reflected evaluations already, what we think is to come.
turns.zh: 所以它也给了我们一种防守的方式。我们认为某些领域，比如半导体的某些部分，已经跑在了基本面前面，或者说已经反映了我们认为未来才会兑现的东西。

turns.en: Then we have the picks and shovels. We have power and resources. They are the investing opportunities set, industrials, utilities and materials.
turns.zh: 然后是卖铲子的环节，电力与资源（power and resources）。那里的投资机会是工业、公用事业和材料。

turns.en: We pivoted early in the year, for example, in that portfolio into the materialist sector, because we require so many resources, commodities for that built out.
turns.zh: 比如今年早些时候，我们就在那个组合里转向了材料板块，因为建设需要消耗那么多资源和大宗商品。

turns.en: And then lastly, longevity. We think in particular, US farmer is going to be a beneficiary of AI. It's not going to be fast. This is a lot more complex biochemistry than just solving a math problem.
turns.zh: 最后是长寿。我们尤其认为美国的 pharma（制药业）会成为 AI 的受益者。但不会很快——这比解一道数学题要复杂得多的生物化学。

turns.en: We are still trying to understand how the human cell works. Now we're starting to see more models that are trying to understand that. But I think we have seen the green shoots.
turns.zh: 我们到现在还在试图理解人体细胞是怎么工作的。现在我们才开始看到更多试图理解它的模型。但我认为我们已经看到了破土而出的嫩芽。

turns.en: We now have the first drug in phase three clinical trials in the US. There are many AI discovered drugs that are already in phase two. So we think this is a very, very interesting area to invest in.
turns.zh: 我们现在已经有第一款药物在美国进入三期临床试验，还有很多 AI 发现的药物已经在二期。所以我们认为这是非常、非常值得投资的方向。

turns.en: But what we have seen in the market, Dean, is that on days where the semiconductor trade, the AI enabling trade is selling off, we have seen other parts of our trios, in particular the longevity one, which right now is heavily focused on farmer, be a ballast and actually showing performance positive return on those days.
turns.zh: 但我们在市场上看到的现象是，Dean，每当半导体交易、AI 使能交易被抛售的那些天，我们三驾马车里的其他部分——尤其是长寿，目前重仓 pharma——反而起到了压舱石的作用，甚至在那些天录得了正收益。

turns.en: So I think it's a good illustration of how you can play offense and defense at the same time by just choosing how you are positioned inside the individual portfolios, but also how do you structure them as one more broader transformational innovation portfolio?
turns.zh: 所以我认为这是一个很好的例证：通过选择你在单个组合内部的布局方式，以及如何把它们组织成一个更宽泛的变革性创新组合，你可以同时打进攻和防守。

turns.en: We live in this environment in which the macro forces seem everywhere, whether it's the geopolitical instability, we talk about rates and inflation.
turns.zh: 我们生活在一个宏观力量似乎无处不在的环境里，不管是地缘政治的不稳定，还是我们一直在谈的利率和通胀。

turns.en: Those are macro. They would seem to impact the equity market from a causing stocks to be more correlated if the back end of the bond market has a bad day that would seem bad for markets in general.
turns.zh: 这些都是宏观。它们似乎会从因果上冲击股票市场，让股票相关性升高——如果债市长端过得很糟糕，对整个市场来说似乎都是坏消息。

turns.en: And yet the day-to-day correlations are very low. It's almost as if the S&P 500 internally diversifies itself. And yet from a risk management standpoint, trying to really stress test our portfolios to ensure that we haven't found ourselves long hidden correlations, kind of a universal theme that's just not obvious.
turns.zh: 然而日间的相关性却很低，几乎像是标普 500 在内部自我分散。但从风险管理的角度，真正压力测试我们的组合，确保自己没有做多隐藏的、并不明显的相关性，几乎是一个共通的命题。

turns.en: And on one of your recent podcast, Signal Over Noise, I really enjoyed the way you framed out this portfolio that nominally or optically looks diversified.
turns.zh: 在你最近一期 Signal Over Noise 播客里，我特别喜欢你对这个表面上分散良好的组合的拆解方式。

turns.en: It's got utilities in it. It's got REITs in it. It's got some AI in it. It's got some commodities in it. And you walk through how these are linked and they could be linked kind of after the fact.
turns.zh: 里面有公用事业，有 REIT，有 AI，有大宗商品。你讲清楚了它们是怎么被关联起来的，或者说事后是怎么被同一个因子绑在一起的。

turns.en: I think what you're doing is you're pushing the conversation towards, we've got to really take a look at our portfolio to make sure we don't have hidden exposures.
turns.zh: 我觉得你在把讨论推向一个方向：我们真的得重新审视自己的组合，确保没有隐藏的暴露。

turns.en: I'd love to just move to that discussion and just get you to talk big picture about your efforts there and specifically this exercise that you ran through on the podcast.
turns.zh: 我很想进入这个话题，请你泛泛谈谈你们在这些方面做的努力，特别是你在播客里演示的那次演练。

turns.en: Like you mentioned, I think in portfolio construction, I think one of the biggest risks is overlooking hidden factors. That's why I just want to go back to this three lens framework.
turns.zh: 就像你提到的，我觉得在组合构建里，最大的风险之一就是忽视隐藏因子。这也是为什么我要回到这个三镜头框架。

turns.en: That's why specifically we try to start with that to make sure we cover as many angles as possible. And I think when we look at standards, macro risk models, even if you think about the total portfolio approach and what's typically used in order to construct that, it's very much focused on large macro economic indicators like growth, like inflation, real rates.
turns.zh: 这正是我们特意从它开始的原因，确保覆盖尽可能多的角度。我觉得我们看那些标准的宏观风险模型，甚至你想想全组合方法（total portfolio approach）以及通常用什么来构建它——它们非常聚焦于增长、通胀、实际利率这类大的宏观经济指标。

turns.en: But what seems to have become the driver to your point right now is that actually some of these secular trends, structural trends have become macro factors, yet they are missing in most of the standard models.
turns.zh: 但正如你指出的，现在真正变成驱动因素的，恰恰是这些长期趋势、结构性趋势已经成为宏观因子，而它们在大多数标准模型里是缺席的。

turns.en: And the AI factor in our view needs to be a key element to stress test portfolios. Because if you just look at asset class buckets, you could easily think you're well diversified.
turns.zh: 而 AI 因子，在我们看来，需要成为压力测试组合的关键要素。因为如果你只看资产类别的格子，你很容易觉得自己已经分散得很好。

turns.en: If, for example, you own a large cap tech stock, you own a utility, you own a real estate investment trust, you own emerging markets and your own commodities.
turns.zh: 举例来说，你持有一只大盘科技股，一只公用事业股，一只房地产投资信托，一只新兴市场，还有大宗商品。

turns.en: That looks on the surface if you do a pie chart by asset class like a well diversified portfolio. Yet, when you look underneath the surface, they all have one common hidden factor.
turns.zh: 表面上看，如果按资产类别做一张饼图，那像是一个分散良好的组合。然而往水面之下看，它们全部共享一个隐藏的因子。

turns.en: And that is AI. The hyperscalers, the large cap tech companies are profiting from all the spend through the cloud computing. The utilities are profiting from it because of the increased power demand, in particular the independent power producers.
turns.zh: 那就是 AI。超大规模云厂商、大盘科技公司通过云计算从所有的支出中获利。公用事业也在获利，因为电力需求上升，尤其是独立发电商（independent power producers）。

turns.en: Then you have, of course, commodities, which are being also used in order to construct these data centers. Data center reads are exposed because they're part of the built out.
turns.zh: 然后是大宗商品，它们也在被用于建设这些数据中心的建设。数据中心 REIT 也有暴露，因为它们本身就是建设的一部分。

turns.en: And then lastly, emerging markets. I've been dominated by three stocks. And those stocks are all semiconductor companies that are very key to the build out of the data centers.
turns.zh: 最后是新兴市场，它被三只股票主导，而那三只全是半导体公司，对数据中心建设至关重要。

turns.en: So the one variable that they all have in common is AI capital expenditures. And I think that is critical to include in any scenario analysis that you're now running on portfolios and potential downside risk that could come from the AI spending trajectory.
turns.zh: 所以它们唯一共有的变量就是 AI 资本开支。我认为这一点对现在跑在任何组合上的情景分析、以及 AI 支出轨迹可能带来的下行风险，都至关重要。

turns.en: What is that AI factor that you superimpose a shock of some kind to do it on the rate side or the inflation side? That's been done for a long time.
turns.zh: 那个 AI 因子长什么样？你叠加的冲击是做什么？是做在利率端还是通胀端？这些已经被做了很长时间。

turns.en: Those econometric models in terms of how those macro factors feed into the economy. What does an AI factor look like? I mean, when we think about AI, we think about NVIDIA and we think about the hyperscalers and so forth in terms of the construction of that factor and the way in which you would basically superimpose a shock on a portfolio and its impact.
turns.zh: 那些计量经济学模型讲的是宏观因子如何传导进经济。那么 AI 因子又是什么样子？我们说 AI 会想到 NVIDIA，会想到超大规模云厂商等等——从那个因子的构建方式，到如何对组合叠加冲击以及影响。

turns.en: Walk us through that a little bit more specifically. There are three ways to think about the AI risk factors. One is the supply bottlenecks.
turns.zh: 带我们讲得再具体一点。——思考 AI 风险因子有三个角度。第一是供给瓶颈。

turns.en: We just discussed that. I think the supply bottlenecks are going to be temporary. There you position in the areas that are most scarce because those companies will have pricing power and can absorb that in the best possible way.
turns.zh: 我们刚才讨论过。我认为供给瓶颈会是暂时的。在瓶颈里，你要配置在最稀缺的环节，因为那些公司会有定价权，能以最好的方式消化。

turns.en: But it'll be transitory because we will come up with more supply over time. This for me is more you have a super exponential curve on AI, but you have just linear restrictions that we impose as humans.
turns.zh: 但它是过渡性的，因为我们最终会给出更多供给。对我来说这更像是：AI 是一条超指数曲线，而我们人类施加的约束只是线性的。

turns.en: We cannot grow super exponentially. We cannot self-learn as AI can. And therefore, at some point, there's going to be a crossover point where AI continues to accelerate and any of these components of the value chain, which are subject to just the linearity of us as humans will hit.
turns.zh: 我们人类做不到超指数增长，也做不到像 AI 那样自学。所以到某个时点一定会有一个交叉点，AI 继续加速，而价值链上那些受制于人类线性能力的环节会撞上这个点。

turns.en: But again, temporary demand is a little bit trickier because there, if there is at some point a gap between what the market perceives as the monetization trajectory and a potential expectation gap, that could cause more ripple effects in the markets because everything right now in terms of financing agreements.
turns.zh: 不过前面说过是暂时的。需求稍微更棘手一点，因为那里如果到了某个时点，市场感知的变现轨迹与预期之间出现缺口，可能会在市场里引起更大的涟漪，因为现在围绕融资协议的一切……

turns.en: A lot of people call out the circular financing agreements that that's a risk. It's not a risk in my mind as a catalyst. The catalyst will be if demand disappoints.
turns.zh: 很多人把循环融资协议（circular financing agreements）点名为风险。但在我眼里，它作为催化剂不是风险。催化剂是需求如果令人失望。

turns.en: So far, we don't see signs of that. But if demand disappoints, these constructs will just mean that there's more downside because more players will be impacted.
turns.zh: 到目前为止我们没看到那种迹象。但如果需求让人失望，这些结构只会意味着更大的下行，因为被波及的玩家更多。

turns.en: It's the same thing with valuations. Valuations themselves are not a catalyst for market correction. It's a fundamental disappointment. That's the catalyst and valuations just tell you how much the market is likely going to fall and corrupt.
turns.zh: 估值也是一样。估值本身不是市场修正的催化剂，基本面的失望才是催化剂。估值只是告诉你，市场大概会跌多深。

turns.en: So it gives you a gauge of the downside. And I see it in the same way with these circular deals that, by the way, are not new. They have existed for well over 100 years when you look at developers and landowners and how they have often done similar type of deals.
turns.zh: 所以它给你的是一个下行幅度的标尺。我对这些循环交易也是这么看的——顺便说，它们并不新鲜。你去看地产开发商和土地拥有者的历史，类似交易已经存在了一百多年。

turns.en: Intel has done so many of these deals over the last decades. So not unprecedented, but because the scale of course now is so much larger. I think they take a lot more in terms of attention and bandwidth in the media.
turns.zh: Intel 在过去几十年里做过很多这类交易。所以并非前所未有，只是因为现在的规模大得多，我认为它们就占据了多得多的关注度和媒体的版面。

turns.en: Demand is going to be critical at this point. We don't see demand at all being capped, but at some point there could be constraints. There could be economic constraints or just expectation misses.
turns.zh: 需求在现阶段会是最关键的。我们完全没看到需求封顶，但到了某个时点可能有约束，可能有经济上的约束，或者只是预期落空。

turns.en: If we look at the appreciation of public and private markets that are associated with AI, maybe it's about 25 trillion, that's sort of a rough estimate.
turns.zh: 如果我们看公开和私募市场里跟 AI 相关的市值增值，大概是 25 万亿美元，算是一个粗略估计。

turns.en: The value creation from AI, if you think about the revenues directly generated from AI are probably in the application, they are less than a trillion.
turns.zh: 而 AI 真正的价值创造——如果你直接看 AI 产生的收入，在应用层面，可能还不到 1 万亿。

turns.en: It's probably less about the ROI of AI. It's more about whether the market discounts the benefits from AI too quickly, maybe too aggressively and without any friction.
turns.zh: 问题可能更少在于 AI 的投资回报率，而在于市场是不是太快、也许太激进地、而且假设没有任何摩擦地把 AI 的收益贴现进了价格。

turns.en: I think that will be the question on the demand side. But in a situation like this, again, balanced in the portfolio can also come from parts that are typically uncorrelated with the more growthy areas of the market such as healthcare and also consumer staples.
turns.zh: 我觉得那将是需求侧的问题。但在这种情形下，组合里的平衡也可以来自通常与市场高成长部分不相关的板块，比如医疗健康和必需消费（consumer staples）。

turns.en: And UBS also like quality as a factor, quality businesses in those industries and data staples. You have companies that have very stable and predictable earnings, where also visibility into earnings is independent of an AI built out.
turns.zh: UBS 也喜欢质量（quality）这个因子，这些行业和必需消费里的优质企业。它们盈利非常稳定、可预测，而且盈利的可见性与 AI 建设无关。

turns.en: So those are areas of the market that could be balanced. And of course, on the fixed income side, we like short duration. We already talked about it.
turns.zh: 所以这些是可以提供平衡的市场部分。当然在固收这边，我们偏好短久期。我们之前也聊到了。

turns.en: We see risk in the back end and that's a place where across all risk scenarios, whether it's rates, whether it's AI, you mentioned geopolitics, where we think there is the real balanced.
turns.zh: 我们看到长端的风险。而在所有风险情景里，不管是利率、AI，还是你提到的地缘政治，短端是我们认为真正能提供平衡的地方。

turns.en: It doesn't play offense. You really play defense with short term treasury, but it's a good place to be. That gives you optionality in case there are disruptions and in case there are sell-offs to also play offense at that point in time.
turns.zh: 它不是进攻——用短期国债你打的确实是防守——但那是个很好的栖身之处。它给你期权价值：万一出现扰动、出现抛售，你到时也有本钱去进攻。

turns.en: Time is always a source of uncertainty in markets and in life. So you mentioned the kind of short part of the yield curve. Maybe it's twos. People look at the twos 10 spread, twos 30 spread.
turns.zh: 时间永远是市场和人生里的不确定性来源。所以你提到了收益率曲线的短端，可能是 2 年期——大家会看 2 年对 10 年、2 年对 30 年的利差。

turns.en: So you get some pickup for extending out to 10 or 30. But boy, I would argue not enough just in the sense that those additional eight plus years is a lifetime away in this type of environment where the pace of change is just so aggressive.
turns.zh: 拉长到 10 年或者 30 年你确实能捡到一些收益。但我要说不够——在这种变化速度极其激进的环境里，多出来的那八年以上漫长得像一辈子。

turns.en: Really what investors are trying to price is some expected value where possibly the right tail is just outlandishly high in a good way. These are options, but the challenge, and this is where I'd love for you to help me understand this a little bit more, is you have to pull forward a lot of the potential benefits where markets are pricing in expected values and their entertaining scenarios that could be extremely high, returns that could be astronomical.
turns.zh: 投资者真正想定价的，是一种期望值，而那个右尾可能好到高得离谱。这些本质上是期权。但难点在于，这也是我很想请你帮我再多理解一点的地方：你必须把很多潜在收益提前贴现。市场在定价期望值，并且在想象一些可能极高的情景、可能天文数字的回报。

turns.en: And then the challenge becomes, and this is where I would love for you to give us some of your thought process around how do investors ultimately price in the use case of adoption?
turns.zh: 于是挑战就变成了——这块我很想听听你的思路——投资者最终如何把用例（use case）和采用（adoption）定价进去？

turns.en: Is there the potential that the corporate adoption side just takes longer than people expect? Ultimately, corporates have to benefit from this a tremendous amount.
turns.zh: 有没有可能，企业采用这一端就是比大家预期的慢？最终，企业必须从中获得巨大的收益。

turns.en: How does that tension look like? Where we're pricing in potentially amazing scenarios, but at some point there's got to be a handoff where the profitability side is viewed as acceptably arrived, where it's here, and we're not just pricing in potentially future incredible outcomes?
turns.zh: 这种张力怎么呈现？我们正在定价一些可能非常美妙的情景，但到某个时点必须完成交接棒——盈利这一端要被视为可以接受的、已经到位的状态，而不是一直在定价未来的惊人结果。

turns.en: It's a very fair point. I think probably just reference wasn't the public domain, but there have been references to the inference workloads now being profitable for the frontier models.
turns.zh: 这是个非常中肯的点。我想可能——那些参考虽然不在公共领域——已经有信息说推理（inference）工作负载现在对前沿模型来说是有利润的。

turns.en: And I think this is very important and also backed up, by the way, from a public blog post that deep sea growth last year about actually seeing quite decent growth margins for inference.
turns.zh: 我觉得这一点非常重要，而且顺便说，DeepSeek 去年公开的博客文章也佐证了这一点，他们实际上看到了相当不错的推理毛利。

turns.en: Once you have optimized the stack, that tells you that there is a case where you can see profitability over time. More and more of AI will be inference, especially as we approach AGI.
turns.zh: 一旦你把整个技术栈优化好，它告诉你的是：随着时间推移是可以看到盈利的。AI 中越来越多会是推理，尤其在接近 AGI 的时候。

turns.en: We don't need to train the models as much anymore at that point, and it will just be about AI usage. If we can establish that inference is profitable from a gross margin and an operating margin perspective, I think the market will underwrite that and will underwrite the trajectory from here.
turns.zh: 到那时我们不再需要那么多训练模型，剩下的就是 AI 的使用。如果我们能确立推理从毛利润率到营业利润率都是盈利的，我认为市场会为它背书，会认可以后的轨迹。

turns.en: If that for whatever reason gets questioned, I think that would be another very big risk factor. But again, we have some evidence, and the math is, again, public on GitHub.
turns.zh: 如果这一点因为任何原因受到质疑，我觉得那会是一个非常大的风险因素。但同样，我们已经有一些证据，而且相关的计算又是公开在 GitHub 上的。

turns.en: I think deep sea called it one more thing in reference to the famous Steve Jobs quote, but it's not just one more thing. It's probably the thing.
turns.zh: 我想 DeepSeek 还提到了一件事，呼应乔布斯那句有名的 One more thing——但它恐怕不只是 one more thing，它就是那个 the thing。

turns.en: The question that you asked is that if inference is profitable, we can underwrite the trajectory because we know that we don't need less of AI at any point in time.
turns.zh: 你刚才那个问题的意思是：如果推理是赚钱的，我们就可以为这条轨迹背书，因为我们知道在任何时点我们都不会需要更少的 AI。

turns.en: We will only need more. There's almost an infinite amount of problems that we still need to solve as humans. The cheaper it gets, the more there is, the more productivity gains we'll see and the more economic growth.
turns.zh: 我们只会需要更多。作为人类，待解决的问题几乎是无限的。它越便宜、越多，我们看到的生产力增益就越多，经济增长就越多。

turns.en: So I think that remains the North Star, and that's why our base case still is that we are going to see an increase in AI capex for the foreseeable future.
turns.zh: 所以我认为那仍然是北极星，我们的基准情形依然是：在可预见的未来，AI 资本开支还会继续增加。

turns.en: In our view, it's going to be 1.2 trillion next year already. But if you sum up, if you look into 2030, you're right that we are going to be raising, whether it's through equity or debt, another multiple of trillion dollars, four, potentially five trillion in additional capital to get to the amount of AI compute that we need to cater to those workloads.
turns.zh: 在我们看来，明年就会达到 1.2 万亿美元。但如果你加总一下，看到 2030 年，你说得对，不管通过股权还是债务，我们要再融资好几万亿，可能是四万亿甚至五万亿美元的增量资本，才能达到服务这些工作负载所需的 AI 算力。

turns.en: We see, I wrote a paper where we tried to compute the floating point operations per second flops that we'll need by 2030 in order to cater to all the AI demand.
turns.zh: 我们看到——我写过一篇论文，尝试计算到 2030 年我们需要多少 FLOPS（每秒浮点运算次数，floating point operations per second）才能满足所有的 AI 需求。

turns.en: Just by looking at inference, just by looking at enterprise consumer agentic AI, not even considering physical AI and what we may see there.
turns.zh: 只看推理，只看企业级、消费级和 agentic AI（智能体 AI），甚至都还没考虑物理 AI 以及我们可能在那里看到的东西。

turns.en: We estimate that we need five times the amount of compute that we had installed at the end of last year. So a lot of upside in stent, again, the biggest risk is bottlenecks on the supply side, but the trajectory is only going to be going in one way and that is up.
turns.zh: 我们估算，需要的算力是去年年底已装机量的五倍。所以上行空间很大——同样，最大的风险是供给侧瓶颈，但轨迹只会朝一个方向走，那就是向上。

turns.en: We do not foresee that at some point we need less capex in order to power these data centers, at least not for the foreseeable future. As the market responds to whether it's specific growth rates for adoption, whether it's usage, those are economic drivers of how the market discounts future profitability.
turns.zh: 我们并不预期到了某个时点需要更少的资本开支来为这些数据中心供电，至少可预见的未来不会。市场会回应，不管回应的是采用的增长速率还是使用量，这些都是市场给未来盈利贴现的经济驱动。

turns.en: Market prices move as well because investors are inside the markets and we're just coming across or just coming off a pretty volatile July. You wouldn't really know it looking at the VIX.
turns.zh: 市场价格也会因为投资者身处市场之中而波动。我们刚刚经历了一个相当动荡的七月——光看 VIX 你大概感觉不到。

turns.en: I think it got to 21, but underneath the surface, there was just some gigantic factor rotations, momentum rotations. So the presence of investors in the markets can matter too.
turns.zh: 我觉得它最高到过 21，但水面之下发生了巨大的因子轮动、动量轮动。所以投资者身处市场之中这件事本身也会起作用。

turns.en: We've seen that time and time again. How does a portfolio the size of yours and with, I think, goals of being long term, how do you be aware of the massive volatility that we saw?
turns.zh: 我们一次又一次看到这种情形。像你们这么大、而且目标我认为是长期的组合，怎么去察觉我们看到的那种巨大波动，

turns.en: But stay invested, but be very risk aware as some of these unwinds occur. Planning is always step number one than thinking through scenarios.
turns.zh: 同时又保持在场，并且在这些撤仓行情发生时高度警觉风险？——规划永远是第一步，就是思考各种情景。

turns.en: That's one of the hallmarks of our work in CIO, the scenario of thinking and also using this in order to optimize our portfolios. The second one is robust optimization, just assuming a certain amount of uncertainty and make sure that even if those lower bounds, those risk cases hit that we are still within risk constraints.
turns.zh: 这是我们 CIO 工作的标志之一，情景思维，并用它来优化组合。第二是稳健优化（robust optimization），也就是假设一定的不确定性，确保即使触到那些下限、那些风险情形，我们仍然在风险约束之内。

turns.en: We go back to the three lenses. We define the different scenarios. Also, how these scenarios may interact because typically one thing may kick it off, but then you can very easily have one thing leading to the other.
turns.zh: 我们回到三个镜头，定义不同的情景，也定义这些情景可能如何相互作用。因为通常是一件事引爆，然后很容易一件事接着引出另一件事。

turns.en: I mean, for example, if rates go to a point where financing per capita becomes an issue, of course, that means stress probably in other parts of the private markets also as some companies will be challenged with their dead load.
turns.zh: 比如，如果利率升到某个水平，让单个数据中心的融资成了问题，那当然意味着私募市场其他地方也可能承压，因为一些公司的债务负担会很吃紧。

turns.en: That may mean that there is going to be larger questions about this AI built out, the equity market is going to go down. That will invalidate some of the wealth effects.
turns.zh: 这可能意味着外界会对这轮 AI 建设提出更大的疑问，股票市场会下跌，那又会抵消一部分财富效应。

turns.en: I mean, a lot what we've seen of course, why the economy is so strong also is because of the consumer spending. If that were then to be questioned because of just uncertainty, those are all things that can compound on each other.
turns.zh: 我是说，我们看到经济之所以这么强，很大一部分靠的是消费支出。如果因为不确定性，消费也随之受到质疑——这些事情是会互相加乘的。

turns.en: When we think about constructing portfolios is you have to think about the risk cases in each scenarios, but also how these scenarios may interact.
turns.zh: 我们在构建组合时，既要想每个情景里的风险情形，也要想这些情景可能如何相互作用。

turns.en: So building in robustness to downside cases is very important. But it's also important that while you're long term oriented that you have enough flexibility on the short time frame to make sure you can make adjustments.
turns.zh: 所以对下行情形建立稳健性非常重要。但同样重要的是，尽管你以长期为导向，也要在短期尺度上保有足够的灵活性，确保你能够做调整。

turns.en: We do that inside these equity portfolios, but we also do it in the tactical asset allocation through different adjustments to our exposures.
turns.zh: 我们在这些股票组合内部这样做，也在战术资产配置里通过调整敞口这样做。

turns.en: So two ways, you know, inside active portfolios, but also inside how portfolios are structured. We've been mostly talking about AI and the investment opportunity set for AI.
turns.zh: 所以两个层面：主动组合的内部，以及组合结构本身。——我们大部分时间都在聊 AI 和 AI 的投资机会版图。

turns.en: It's a huge factor in markets, as you said, but AI is also a tool to be used for investors. And as someone with a PhD and background in data science and analytics, I'd love to learn a little bit more about how the advent and growth of these incredible tools from a data analytics standpoint.
turns.zh: 就像你说的，它是市场里的一个巨大因子，但 AI 也是投资者可以利用的工具。作为拥有博士学位、有数据科学和分析背景的人，我很想了解一下，这些强大工具在数据分析维度上的出现和成长——

turns.en: How have those changed your investment process? How have they opened up new areas for you to explore and test that may not have even existed a decade ago or five years ago?
turns.zh: 它们如何改变了你们的投资流程？为你们打开了哪些十年前甚至五年前可能都不存在的新领域去探索和检验？

turns.en: AI has certainly changed the way you can analyze things in quite profound ways, especially of course, a genetic AI where you can now ask agents to do certain subtasks for you and help orchestrate big research reports.
turns.zh: AI 无疑已经相当深刻改变了你做分析的方式，尤其是 agentic AI（智能体 AI），你现在可以让智能体替你完成某些子任务、帮你统筹大型研究报告。

turns.en: It does do a lot in terms of collecting information, presenting information, reason through information. So it helps the research process quite dramatically.
turns.zh: 它在收集信息、呈现信息、对信息做推理方面做了很多，所以对研究流程的帮助非常大。

turns.en: In terms of portfolio construction, we go back to the more traditional tools, whether it's some form of, of course, mean variance optimization, or whether it's thinking about using predictive models on the one side or on the factor models.
turns.zh: 至于组合构建，我们用的还是更传统的工具，不管是某种形式的均值-方差优化（mean-variance optimization），还是考虑使用预测模型，或者因子模型。

turns.en: We have found them to be still quite relevant, but at the same time, we think that over time, of course, Gen AI will also be coming up with its own stock models, full slate of quantitative models, taking in both quantitative data, but also so versatile being able to take in text and unstructured data.
turns.zh: 我们发现它们依然相当有用。但同时我们认为，随着时间推移，Gen AI（生成式 AI）当然也会发展出自己的选股模型、整套量化模型——既消化量化数据，也因其通用性而能吃进文本和非结构化数据。

turns.en: It's just a question of time, but at this point, and you mentioned it earlier, perspective and experience do matter in our view and asking the right questions, looking for hidden factors, thinking maybe outside of pattern recognition.
turns.zh: 这只是时间问题。但就当下而言——你之前也提到了——在我们看来，视角和经验确实重要：问对问题、寻找隐藏因子、在模式识别之外去思考。

turns.en: That's where we still think at this point, the human adds value, but we are cognizant that we are in very close competition with what's going to be built with AI.
turns.zh: 我们认为那仍然是此刻人类创造价值的地方。但我们清楚，我们与 AI 将要构建出来的能力之间的竞争已经非常接近。

turns.en: At the same time, when it comes to just understanding our clients and their needs and how we can optimize all of these things solistically, that's where I think the real value comes in.
turns.zh: 与此同时，说到理解我们的客户及其需求、如何从整体上优化这一切——我觉得那才是真正价值的来源。

turns.en: Understanding the risk appetite, understanding the needs and making sure we can put together something through a holistic perspective of a portfolio and client needs where I think the human will maybe become even more important over time.
turns.zh: 理解风险偏好，理解需求，确保我们能通过对组合与客户需求的整体视角把它们组装起来——在这个环节，我认为人类随着时间推移甚至可能变得更重要。

turns.en: Trust is that one variable that is very difficult, I think, to replace. I say this often, there's alpha in trust and it's a uniquely human to human asset that's valuable.
turns.zh: 信任是唯一一个我认为极难被替代的变量。我经常说这句话：信任里有 alpha（there's alpha in trust）——它是独一无二的人与人之间的资产，非常有价值。

turns.en: I was going to end with trying to get some of your perspective on younger folks that might be interested in coming into this industry, the financial services industry, whether it's managing money, whether it's doing research.
turns.zh: 我本来想以这个话题收尾：请你给年轻人一些建议——那些可能有意进入我们这个行业、金融服务行业的人，不管是管理资金，还是做研究。

turns.en: We live in this era in which things are changing so quickly. There's a tremendous amount of technology in front of us. What are the attributes of a younger person that might be just coming out of school that is seeking to get into this business?
turns.zh: 我们生活在一个变化极快的时代，面前有海量技术。一个刚走出校园、想进入这行的年轻人，应该具备什么特质？

turns.en: What are some of the things that you're looking for that you would recommend that they focus on as they pursue a career in markets? I would encourage them to look into a career in markets.
turns.zh: 你在寻找什么样的素质？对想在市场里发展事业的人，你有什么建议？——我会鼓励他们考虑进入市场这个领域。

turns.en: I think there is nothing that's more interesting because you always have to imagine the future and what's more compelling than that than imagining the future, whether it's on where you position from an investing from a return lens or to think about how you manage risk.
turns.zh: 我觉得没有比这更有意思的事了，因为你必须永远想象未来——还有比想象未来更吸引人的吗？无论你是从投资和回报的视角思考往哪里布局，还是思考怎么管理风险，

turns.en: It's probably the purest intellectual pursuit outside of academia. Well, Rurike, it's been a pleasure to host this conversation. Thank you so much.
turns.zh: 它可能都是学术界之外最纯粹的一种智力追求。——好，Ulrike，非常荣幸主持了这场对话，太感谢了。

turns.en: I'm really glad we had a chance to sit down. Really enjoyed the conversation. Thank you so much for having me on. You've been listening to the Alpha Exchange.
turns.zh: 我真的很高兴我们有机会坐下来好好聊，我非常享受这次对话，谢谢你邀请我来。——您刚才收听的是 Alpha Exchange。

turns.en: If you've enjoyed the show, please do tell a friend. And before we leave, I wanted to invite you to drop us some feedback as we aim to utilize these conversations to contribute to the investment community's understanding of risk.
turns.zh: 如果您喜欢这档节目，请推荐给一位朋友。在我们结束之前，我想邀请您给我们留一些反馈，因为我们希望用这些对话为投资界理解风险尽一份力。

turns.en: Your input is valuable and provides direction on where we should focus. Please email us at feedback at alphaexchangepodcast.com. Thanks again and catch you next time.
turns.zh: 您的意见很有价值，也为我们指明该把精力投向哪里。请发邮件到 feedback at alphaexchangepodcast.com。再次感谢，下期再见。
